newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq slams U.N over Turkish incursion.
newsitem.headline: Iraq slams U.N over Turkish incursion.

text.p: Iraqi Deputy Prime Minister Tareq Aziz accused the U.N. Security Council of being "indifferent" to the Turkish incursion in northern Iraq, the official news agency said on Tuesday.

"The head of the council and its members have failed so far to take any measure against the invasion except a short statement by the secretary-general," Aziz said in a letter to the chairman of the Security Council carried by the Iraqi News Agency.
Thousands of Turkish troops poured into northern Iraq earlier this month in pursuit of separatist guerrillas of the Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK).
U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan condemned the incursion and urged Ankara to pull out its troops.
"Such an indifferent stand taken by the Security Council toward such a serious event raises questions on the decisions adopted by the council toward Iraq," he said.
Aziz called the invasion a "flagrant and serious violation of Iraq's sovereignty, integrity and national security and a serious violation of international law and the U.N. charter."
